G OR WINNIE E.' street label and the 'SEE SHEET No. 27' caption. Sheet 27's paper starts at x=40-50 but it draws nothing west of the Av. G EAST property line at x = 220.40 - 0.00227*(y-2000) (rms 1.5 px over 2590 rows); west of it there is only '70'', 'AV. G OR WINNIE E.' and 'SEE SHEET No 10.'. No building, lot, block, hydrant or gallery is drawn twice. All control below is therefore constructed: each sheet's own drawn frontage line of Av. notes:
METHOD. Every feature was identified semantically first (printed street names 22ND ST., 23RD OR TREMONT, 24TH ST., 25TH ST. OR BATH AV., AV. G OR WINNIE E.; block numbers 382/383/384 on sheet 10 and 322/323/324 on sheet 27; named buildings TRINITY CHURCH (EPISCOPAL), EATON MEMORIAL CHAPEL, GERMAN LUTHERAN CHURCH + SCHOOL, E.E. SEIXAS CARRIAGE FACTORY on sheet 27, and the BAKERY/FIRE ALM BOX corner on sheet 10) and only then measured. No template matching, NCC or feature matching was used anywhere. Crops with a 1-source-pixel grid at known source coordinates are in output/qc/manual_crops/ (OV_*, A_*, B*_*, C1*, D_*, P0/P2/P3/P7_*, Q2-Q6_*, R_*).

MEASUREMENT. The two Av. G frontage lines were fitted over 2236 / 2590 rows (rms 1.72 / 1.51 px). The seven cross-street property lines were located from darkness-weighted column centroids in a 96 px window immediately adjacent to the seam, with the line bearing fixed at the sheet-pooled value obtained by tracking each property line right across the sheet (+0.082 deg on sheet 10, +0.204 deg on sheet 27; per-line scatter 0.05 / 0.03 deg). Repeating the intercept with three different windows changes it by <=0.20 px and the along-line rms is 0.09-0.25 px, so the raw measurement precision is far better than the stated uncertainties.

WHAT LIMITS THE UNCERTAINTY is not the measurement. It is (a) the 70 ft transfer to the centreline - a purely systematic x-shift common to all seven points, worth ~3 px if the platted 70 ft is off by 1 ft, which biases tx but almost nothing else; and (b) real paper distortion at the outer edges of both sheets. The sheet-10 right paper edge is visibly curved (x 3353 at y=300 falling to 3324 at y=3600) and the sheet-27 left edge likewise. Points L0 and L6 sit closest to the paper corners and carry the larger stated uncertainties.

TWO THINGS THAT SURPRISED ME AND MATTER TO THE PROJECT. (1) The along-seam scale ratio implied by these seven property lines is 1.00265, but the ratio of the two printed scale bars is 3.0713/3.0456 = 1.00844. That is a 0.58 % disagreement, ~20 px over the 3510 px seam, between the sheet centres (where the scale bars are printed) and the sheet edges (where this seam is). A single global scale per sheet cannot satisfy both; the CHECKPOINT's common-scale prior from the scale bars should be understood as a centre-of-sheet quantity. (2) The independently measured street and block pitches at the seam disagree between the sheets by up to 2.5 % on individual intervals (22nd St reads 80.3 ft on sheet 10 and 81.6 ft on sheet 27 at the seam) while agreeing to 0.3 % on others - a distortion field, not a scale error.

GEOMETRIC CAVEAT FOR THE SOLVER. All seven points lie on the Av. G centreline, so they are collinear to within 3 px (sheet 10) and 8 px (sheet 27). This is fine for a similarity (nullity 0) and the 3510 px baseline determines the relative rotation well, but the across-seam (x) direction carries almost no independent information: the self-check dx residuals are all <0.02 px because the 4-parameter model absorbs them exactly. Do not read the low rms as evidence that the across-seam offset is verified - it is not, and it rests entirely on the printed 70 ft avenue width. There is no way to do better on this seam: neither sheet draws a single building, lot or block belonging to the other.

Self-check similarity is sheet 10 -> sheet 27, weights 1/uncertainty^2, no point rejected; residuals are essentially pure dy: -4.91, +0.16, +1.30, +3.40, -2.00, -0.73, +0.07 px from L0 to L6.
